record.title: Cache-to-Cache reports faster cross-model communication through direct KV-cache transfer
record.summary: The Cache-to-Cache (C2C) paper proposes transferring a source model’s key/value cache into a target model through a learned fuser, bypassing text generation between models. Across four question-answering benchmarks and several Qwen, Llama and Gemma combinations, the authors report 6.4–14.2% higher average accuracy than individual models and about 3.1–5.4% above text-to-text handoffs; latency was 2.5× faster on average in their tested settings. Their detailed timing table reports 3.46×, 1.51× and 14.41× speedups over text handoff for three model pairs. The fuser uses trainable pair-specific components, and scaling to many communicating models with O(N) training cost remains open. These are paper-reported results; no independent reproduction was performed.
organizations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: C2C uses a learned module to project and fuse source and receiver KV caches, with a dynamic weighting mechanism and trainable layer gates.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across four benchmarks, the authors report 6.4–14.2% higher average accuracy than individual models and about 3.1–5.4% higher accuracy than text-to-text communication, with an average 2.5× speedup in their tested settings.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a detailed MMLU-Redux comparison, authors report replacing 80 text handoff tokens and 1,312 ms of decoding with 90 ms of KV-cache fusion; timing used a single A100 with batch size one.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports that a weaker sharer can mislead a receiver, and identifies O(N) fuser training cost for scaling to multiple communicating models as unresolved.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: No independent reproduction or production deployment result was obtained in this review.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent reproduction of accuracy and latency results across model pairs and benchmarks.
End-to-end matched comparison including fuser training, cache transformation overhead, serving costs and realistic multi-turn agent workloads.
Measure transfer robustness, failure containment and audit/security properties of internal-state communication.

brief.importance_rationale: If direct KV-cache transfer gives repeatable accuracy and latency gains across heterogeneous model pairs, it could change multi-model inference and agent communication design. The score reflects architectural potential, not confidence in broad transfer or deployment economics.
limitations: All performance and timing results are reported by the paper authors; no independent replication was performed.
The evaluated tasks are four multiple-choice QA benchmarks with zero-shot, temperature-zero prompts; this does not establish gains on open-ended agent workflows.
Timing uses one NVIDIA A100 at batch size one; end-to-end serving costs and integration constraints are not measured.
A weak or inaccurate sharer can mislead the receiver; the paper includes failure examples.
Pairwise fuser training scales with the number of communicating model pairs; the authors identify O(N) training cost as an open issue.
Direct internal-state transfer is less human-readable than text handoffs; the paper does not evaluate auditability or security implications.
organizations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
brief.summary: The Cache-to-Cache (C2C) paper proposes transferring a source model’s key/value cache into a target model through a learned fuser, bypassing text generation between models. Across four question-answering benchmarks and several Qwen, Llama and Gemma combinations, the authors report 6.4–14.2% higher average accuracy than individual models and about 3.1–5.4% above text-to-text handoffs; latency was 2.5× faster on average in their tested settings. Their detailed timing table reports 3.46×, 1.51× and 14.41× speedups over text handoff for three model pairs. The fuser uses trainable pair-specific components, and scaling to many communicating models with O(N) training cost remains open. These are paper-reported results; no independent reproduction was performed.

technical.claimed_result: Across four benchmarks, authors report 6.4–14.2% higher average accuracy than individual models, approximately 3.1–5.4% over text-to-text communication, and 2.5× average latency speedup. In one MMLU-Redux setup, C2C replaces 80 generated handoff tokens and 1,312 ms of decoding with 90 ms of cache fusion. Results vary substantially by model pair.
technical.compute_or_cost: In the reported MMLU-Redux training analysis, a 300-step fuser checkpoint took under 9 GPU hours and approached the final result for three pairs; full training ranged from 44.72 to 54.24 GPU hours. Reported inference speedups exclude general serving and system-integration costs.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public paper and code link are inspectable. The reported benchmark and timing outcomes are author-run results and have not been independently reproduced in this review.
technical.implementation_status: Paper proposes and evaluates C2C; the linked implementation is public. The fuser is trained for sharer–receiver combinations. Scaling to many communicating models with O(N) training cost is described as an open problem.
technical.mechanism: A learned fuser projects the source model’s KV cache into the receiver’s representation and combines it with receiver state using dynamic weights and per-layer gates; model weights are frozen while the fuser is trained. Token and layer alignment support different tokenizers, model families and sizes.
technical.novelty: Uses model KV caches for direct cross-model semantic transfer, with a learned conversion/fusion module, instead of serializing an intermediate message as generated text.
technical.regime: Research-scale experiments with Qwen2.5/Qwen3, Llama3.2 and Gemma3 models from 0.6B to 14B parameters, four QA benchmarks, a 500k-sample OpenHermes2.5 training subset for fusers, and an A100 timing setup. No production multi-tenant or multi-agent deployment is measured.
technical.reproducibility: The paper provides experimental details and links code, but the research desk did not execute or independently reproduce it. Benchmark methodology and author-reported results remain subject to replication.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares C2C with text-to-text collaboration, query-level routing, and each sharer/receiver alone. Evaluations use zero-shot prompts at temperature zero and report four knowledge/reasoning benchmarks; inference timing uses one NVIDIA A100 at batch size one.

brief.title: Cache-to-Cache reports faster cross-model communication through direct KV-cache transfer
brief.why_it_matters: C2C treats model internal state as a communication medium rather than converting it to readable text. If its reported gains transfer, multi-model systems could avoid serial decoding overhead and transfer information that text handoffs lose. The design also creates a less inspectable channel and requires learned alignment/fusion; the paper’s results are benchmark-bounded and pairwise training cost remains a scaling issue.
